task.title: Resolve auto-fetch URLs with a real parser instead of matching the authority by pattern
task.description: The auto-fetch protection has now failed two independent reviews for the same underlying reason, so this is a third approach and not a third patch. A reviewer adjudicated a forty-eight case matrix against a WHATWG URL oracle and found seventeen bypasses with zero false positives, in five classes the current matcher cannot reach: backslash authority spellings such as a doubled backslash, a scheme followed by backslashes, and a slash-backslash pair; runs of extra slashes after the scheme; the HTML5 named references for tab and newline; the image tag, which the HTML specification aliases to img; and markdown angle-bracket destinations whose whitespace the extraction regexes truncate before the URL is ever classified. Eight reproduce at the MCP tool dispatch with a non-error result, a redaction state of none and the attacker host intact, with advisory redaction disabled; three are byte-identical through the persistence materializer and the tool-output seam. The root cause named by the reviewer is that host recognition pattern-matches the authority rather than resolving it. Replace that with a real URL resolution against a synthetic base, so the classifier sees what a renderer would see, and keep masking on the original byte offsets. Enumerate every auto-fetch surface and every extraction regex that can truncate a destination before classification, and fix the extraction as well as the classification: a bypass that never reaches the classifier is not fixed by improving the classifier. Add the image tag alias. Regression first, driven by the reviewer's matrix: use T24-recheck2-exfil.ts to reproduce all forty-eight cases before you change anything, and keep the four benign controls and the twenty previously fixed vectors passing. Write T40-spec.md before coding, then T40-implementation.md and T40-result.json. Do not review your own fix.

acceptance_criteria: AC5 (AFC-15): a URL secret is masked and a public Markdown link is not treated as a network send; no field-name or spelling bypass remains.

All seventeen bypasses in the reviewer's matrix are closed and adjudicated against a URL oracle rather than against the previous patterns, with zero false positives on the benign controls; the twenty previously fixed vectors still hold; the closures are verified at the MCP dispatch and the persistence materializer, not only at the detector.

Extraction and classification are both correct: no destination is truncated before classification, and every auto-fetch surface including the image tag alias is enumerated in the report with the method used to enumerate it.

Use the platform URL parser rather than writing a new one, and state explicitly what a synthetic base implies for relative and scheme-relative destinations.
